ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: 3-day history of watery diarrhea (5–6 episodes/day), preceded by two episodes of vomiting; no clear food, medication, or environmental trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Vomiting on day 1, resolved; ongoing diarrhea to present; reports significant dehydration and weakness; no abdominal pain, no blood in stool.
- ENT symptoms: Denies throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, or facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling. No ear pain/hearing changes or neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: None reported.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Current medications:
  • Salbutamol (blue) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (used “infrequently” for asthma).
- Past medical history: Asthma.
- Social context: Lives alone; software engineer; currently off work x 3 days due to illness; drinks alcohol socially, non-smoker.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: Not reported.
- Airway/breathing: No stridor, dyspnea, or noisy breathing reported.
- Mental status: Describes weakness but coherent and oriented; no dizziness or syncope noted.
- Vitals and physical exam: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person: Patient was alone during teleconsultation.

Assessment:
- Presumed acute viral/bacterial gastroenteritis. No ENT involvement identified.

Plan:
- Advise oral rehydration with commercial electrolyte solution (Dioralyte) and liberal clear fluids.
- Symptomatic relief: Paracetamol for fever/weakness (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Rest and continue time off work; may return after 24–48 h diarrhea-free.
- Red flags/escalation: Seek medical attention if unable to keep fluids down, worsening weakness, persistent vomiting, bloody stools, high fever, or any new airway/breathing difficulties.
- Follow-up: Telephone/clinic review in 3–5 days if no improvement; earlier if deterioration.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected: ENT-specific review of airway, voice, swallowing, and facial/oral cavity on exam; vital signs; documentation of salbutamol dosage and frequency; confirmation of auto-injector availability (not indicated but standard ENT allergy check).  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; no significant inaudible sections.
